la:adv:vehementer.html:
vĕhĕmenter (vēmenter), adv.
vehemens
.
(Acc. to vehemens, I.) Eagerly, impetuously, ardently, violently, earnestly, vehemently, etc.: vehementer irata,; : vos credere hoc mihi vehementer velim,: se agere,: quae vehementer, acriter, animose fiunt,: vehementer eos incusavit,: commotus,.—Comp.: insectari aliquem vehementius,: nisi alicui vehementius minari,: vehementius equos incitare,.—Sup.: vehementissime contendere,: proeliari, Auct. B. G. 8, 30: vehementissime sibi animum ad virtutem adcendi,. —
(Acc. to vehemens, II.) Strongly, forcibly, powerfully, exceedingly, extremely, very much: fluctuare video vehementer mare,: astringere manus,; cf. ; : vehementer id retinebatur,: hoc te vehementer etiam atque etiam rogo,, D: displicere,: quod vehementer ad has res Attinet,: (res) vehementer ad me pertinet, Cael. ap. : vitium vehementer effugere,.— Comp.: ingemere vehementer,.—Sup.: se vehementissime exercere in aliquā re,: probare, Licin. Calv. ap. P.

la:adj:vehemens.html:
vĕhĕmens (veemens, K. and H.; more freq. vēmens, ; ; and Lucr. always, Lachm., Munro), entis, adj.
perh. Sanscr. vahis, out of, and mens; cf. vē-
,
very eager, violent, furious, impetuous, ardent, vehement, etc. (syn. violentus).
Lit.: vehemens in utramque partem, Menedeme, es nimis, Aut largitate nimiā aut parsimoniā,: Galba non in agendo solum, sed etiam in meditando vehemens atque incensus,: in alios, id. Sull. 31, 87: vehemens feroxque naturā,; with severus (opp. lenissimus),; with inexorabilis,; with dissolutus,; with acer,; with fortis,: vehemens lupus et sibi et hosti Iratus pariter,: canis,.—Of abstract things: acer et vehemens incitatio,: genus orationis vehemens atque atrox,: vehemens et pugnax exordium dicendi,: vehemens et aspera quaestio,: vehemens et grave senatusconsultum,. —
Transf., in gen., active, forcible, vigorous, powerful, mighty, strong: satis vemens causa ad objurgandum,: Arcturus signum sum omnium acerrimum: Vehemens sum exoriens: quom occido vehementior,: imber,: vehementior cursus fluminum,: vehementissimus cursus,: fuga,: ictus,: pilum ... vehementius ictu missuque telum,: impetus,: brassica ... tenui suco vehementissima,very powerful, very efficacious,: medicamentum efficacius et vehementius,: vitis vehementioribus statuminibus impedanda est,stronger,: vitis vehemens multaque materia frondens,vigorous,: palus,thick, stout,: violentia vini,: vis frigorum aut calorum,; cf.: vis in oratione vehementissima,: vehementior lethargus,: dolor capitis,: usus strigilis,: argumentum vehementius,: conviva salibus vehemens intra pomoeria natis,.

la:verb:veho.html:
vĕho, xi, ctum, 3, v. a. and n.
Sanscr. vahāmi, conduct; Gr. ὄχος, carriage; ὄχλος, crowd; Germ. Wagen; Engl. wagon; cf. Lat. via, vexo
.
Act., to bear, carry, convey, on the shoulders, by wagon, by horse, by ship, etc. (syn.: fero, gero, porto): quicquid inponas, vehunt,: ille'st oneratus recte et plus justo vehit,: siquidem'st decorum erum vehere servom,: reticulum panis onusto umero,: formica ore cibum,: ille taurus, qui vexit Europam,: uxorem plaustro,; cf.: Tantalides ... Pisaeam Phrygiis equis,: cum triumphantem (Camillum) albi per urbem vexerant equi,; cf.: te, Bacche pater, tuae Vexere tigres,: Troica qui profugis sacra vehis ratibus,: dum caelum stellas, dum vehet amnis aquas,: quodque suo Tagus amne vehit aurum,: quod fugiens semel hora vexit,has brought along, has brought,.—Absol.: navim prospexi, quanti veheret interrogavi,. —Pass., to be carried or borne, to ride, sail, go, etc.: mihi aequom'st dari ... vehicla qui vehar,: visus est in somnis curru quadrigarum vehi,: vehi in essedo,: vectus curru,; : vehi per urbem,: in navibus vehi,: in navi,: navi,: lintribus, Müll.: puppe,: parvā rate,; cf. huc,: navem, ubi vectus fui,; ; ; : in equo,: in niveis victor equis,: nympha vehitur pisce,.—Of other swift motions: ut animal sex motibus veheretur,: apes liquidum trans aethera vectae,.—With acc.: ventis maria omnia vecti,.—
Neutr., to be borne, to ride, sail, etc., upon any thing (rare, and perh. only in the part. pres. and in the gerund): consuli proconsul obviam in equo vehens venit, Quadrig. ap. : per medias laudes quasi quadrigis vehens,: partim scripserunt, qui ovarent, introire solitos equo vehentes,; : cui lectica per urbem vehendi jus tribuit,.
la:verb:veho.inflection: xi, ctum, 3, v. a. and n.

la:noun:vehiculum.gloss: A means of transport; vehicle, conveyance, carriage; wagon, cart; ship.
senses: A means of transport; vehicle, conveyance, carriage; wagon, cart; ship.
An agricultural implement for cutting down grain; reaping-machine.
la:noun:vehiculum.html:
vĕhĭcŭlum, i, n.
veho
,
a means of transport, a carriage, conveyance, vehicle.
Lit.
In gen.: ceterae animantes quae vel sedendi vehiculum praebent, vel, etc.,: mihi aequum est dari vehicula, qui vehar,: junctum vehiculum, i e. drawn by a span, ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
A wagon, cart, .—
A ship: furtorum vehiculum,.—*
Transf., an agricultural implement for cutting down grain, a reaping-machine, .

la:noun:vehementia.html:
vĕhĕmentĭa, ae, f.
id.
(post-Aug.).
Eagerness, fervency, vehemence: Pollio Asinius fuit acris vehementiae,: Gracchi,.—
Strength: odoris,: saporis,; cf. : venarum,i. e. a strong pulse,: linteorum strigilumque,i. e. a copious use,.—
Of language: inter hujus generis et illius superioris vehementiam hoc interest,.
